input.brief: Design Excellence: Philippine maker of custom cabinets and office furniture for corporate, banks, schools, hospitals and government, with AutoCAD layouts, manufacturing and install

direction.name: The split stage
direction.idea: Half the screen never moves. One side is a fixed photograph (or object, or product view) that stays in place for the whole visit; the other side is a calm scrolling column with everything you need to read. The fixed half keeps the feeling present while the reader gets on with the facts, like sitting in the room while reading the menu. As sections pass, the fixed image may quietly change to the one that matches.
direction.composition: Desktop: a two-column page, 50/50 or 45/55. One column is `position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh` and holds a single photograph filling it edge to edge, or the object centred on a flat field. The other column scrolls and holds all content in a single narrow measure (max 46ch) with comfortable padding (48–72px): name and one-line description first, then sections separated by generous space, then contact and footer. Headings in the scrolling column are modest (32–44px). The column grounds differ: photograph on one side, flat paper colour on the other, meeting at a clean vertical edge. On a phone the fixed half becomes a 60svh image at the top that stays sticky behind the first section, then releases.
direction.typography: A text-first setting: a readable serif or a calm sans at 17–19px, with one display size for the name. Left-aligned throughout.
direction.colour: The paper colour of the reading column is chosen against the photograph: a tone taken from its shadows or its lightest area. One ink, optionally one accent ink for links and the action.
direction.imagery: One excellent portrait-orientation photograph for the fixed half, plus three or four more that crossfade in as their sections arrive. Small inline photographs in the reading column are optional and should be few.
direction.richness: A full-height photograph always in view, against a quiet, well-set column of text.
direction.pitfalls: The reading column must be genuinely well typeset, since it is half the page. Do not put cards or grids in it. Check that the fixed image crops well at short viewport heights. In blind tests the commonest complaint was monotony: several screens of the same split with only the text changing. Change what the reading half holds from section to section (a list, a large figure, a table, a full-colour panel, a drawing) and let at least one section break the split and run full width.

hero.name: Inset photograph, crossing wordmark
hero.blueprint: One deep, dark flat field. A tall portrait photograph fills the left 47% of the viewport, inset 20px from the top, left and bottom edges, with a 12px radius and object-fit: cover; it is position: sticky for the length of the page while the right side scrolls. Five text links at 15px sit top-right on a 32px margin, the last of them the single action. There is no logo at the top. In the right half, at 44% of the height and centred on that half's own axis, one supporting sentence in the light ink at 24px on up to three lines, max 26ch. Along the bottom runs the name in lowercase at clamp(120px, 12vw, 200px), light or regular weight, tracking -0.04em, on one line. It starts over the photograph's lower-right corner, overlapping the image by about 10% of the viewport width (z-index above it; mix-blend-mode: difference keeps the letters legible on the picture), and ends flush with the right margin, its baseline 40px above the bottom edge.
hero.mobile: The photograph takes the top 58% of the screen, inset 12px, with the same radius. The name runs under it at 21vw on one line, its ascenders overlapping the photograph's bottom edge by 3vw. The sentence follows at 17px, left-aligned on a 20px margin. Links reduce to a menu word and the action on the top row, set over the photograph.
hero.headline: The name in lowercase on one line, up to 9 characters at this size; a longer name drops to 9vw.

motion.name: Scaling wordmark
motion.description: The giant name responds to the scroll: as the first screen leaves, the wordmark scales down a few percent (or grows from 0.94 to 1 as the footer arrives) on a scroll-linked timeline, so the monument feels heavy. Travel stays under 8%. Static fallback where scroll timelines are unsupported. Recipe: 'Scroll-linked progress' in references/motion.md, animating `scale`.

sections.name: Plain names in columns
sections.blueprint: A typographic list with no logos. The heading, two or three words at 28–32px, sits in columns 1–3 and stays top-aligned with the first row of names. Columns 5–12 hold the names in three or four text columns (`columns: 4; column-gap: 32px`), each name on its own line at 20–22px with leading 1.5, sentence case, in the full ink. Where names fall into kinds (clients, press, partners), each kind starts a new column and its first line names the kind in the softer ink at the same size, so no small labels are needed. Columns are of unequal length and are not balanced; ragged bottoms are intended. Twelve to thirty names work best. There are no boxes, bullets or separators: the column edges and the shared baseline do the organising. Leave 120px above and below.
sections.mobile: The heading leads at 26px. Names follow in two columns at 17px with a 20px gap; each kind begins after a 32px break with its name in the softer ink on the first line. Long names wrap inside their column rather than shrinking.

sections.name: Capabilities as a menu
sections.blueprint: The capabilities are set as a printed menu or price list. One paper-coloured sheet, 520–600px wide and taller than it is wide, sits on a contrasting flat ground, centred or starting at column 2; its top and bottom edges are cut into shallow scallops or a zigzag with clip-path, its sides straight. On it, centred at the top, the heading: two or three words at 44–56px, then 40px of space. Below, items in two or three groups; each group opens with its name at 20px bold. Each item is a row: the name at 19px on the left, a short value on the right (a price, a time, a quantity, 'included'), and between them a leader of round 4px dots (border-bottom: 4px dotted, sitting on the baseline). A description at 15px in the soft ink sits under the name, at most 34ch. 18px between items, 44px between groups.
sections.mobile: The sheet fills the width minus 12px margins and keeps its cut top and bottom edges. Names stay left and values right on one line with the dot leader between; descriptions wrap beneath at 15px. Group names drop to 18px. Padding inside the sheet is 20px.

sections.name: Square plate, spare text
sections.blueprint: One flat field split 50/50, at least 88svh tall. Left half: a single square photograph filling the half's width minus 40px margins, vertically centred, square corners. A large simple shape may be laid over it to turn the photograph into the object it stands for: a ring 86% of its width with a 6px stroke and a small solid dot at the centre makes a record; a notch cut by clip-path makes a ticket stub. Right half, a flex column with space-between: at the top a row of three plain text tabs at 18px (editions, years, variants), the active one in full ink and the others at 40%; in the middle the title, two to four words at 32–40px bold, with a 34ch description 48px below; along the bottom two filled rectangular cells side by side, each half the column wide and 72px tall, acting as the two actions, one in ink and one a tone off the field.
sections.mobile: The square photograph comes first at full width with 16px margins. The tabs sit under it as one row at 17px. Then the title at 28px, the description, and the two action cells stacked, each full width and 60px tall.

sections.name: Itinerary on a slip
sections.blueprint: The process is printed as an itinerary or receipt. One paper-coloured slip 420–480px wide stands on a contrasting flat ground at columns 7–11; its bottom edge is a zigzag cut with clip-path and its top edge is straight. The heading, two to four words at clamp(40px, 4.4vw, 68px), sits in columns 1–5 with a 30ch paragraph, top-aligned with the slip. On the slip, in the text face at 16px with tabular figures: stages grouped under time headings that carry the order ('Monday', 'Midweek', 'Friday'), each heading in bold with 28px above it. Under a heading, two to four rows; each row has what happens on the left, a duration or time on the right, and a leader of round 4px dots between. The final row is inverted, paper-coloured text on a full-width ink bar 44px tall, and states the result: what the reader holds at the end and the total time.
sections.mobile: The heading and paragraph come first. The slip follows at full width minus 16px margins, keeping its zigzag bottom edge. Rows keep left text, dots and right value on one line; long descriptions wrap under the left text. The inverted final row stays full width.

sections.name: Sticky photograph, active list
sections.blueprint: Two columns. The left, columns 1–5, is `position: sticky; top: 12vh` and holds one photograph or object at 4:5, 34vw wide, unframed on the ground. The right, columns 7–11, holds a vertical list of five to nine names (treatments, rooms, courses, services) at clamp(20px, 1.6vw, 24px), each row 58px tall with the name at the left and a price or duration right-aligned at 15px in the soft ink. The active row is full ink; the others rest at 40% opacity. Hovering, focusing or scrolling a row to the middle of the viewport makes it active, crossfades the left photograph to that item's image over 300ms, and opens a three-line description at 15px, 34ch wide, directly under the name, pushing later rows down. A heading of two or three words at clamp(32px, 3.4vw, 48px) sits above the list, aligned to its left edge, 48px above the first row.
sections.mobile: The photograph becomes a 4:3 band pinned to the top of the screen at 38svh while the list scrolls beneath it; the heading sits above the first row. Rows are 56px tall and the description opens on tap. The image changes with the row nearest the band.

sections.name: Last photograph, text beside
sections.blueprint: A final full-bleed photograph, 100vw by 90svh, chosen so its subject sits in the left half and its right half is calm. All text is confined to the right half and never crosses the centre line: in columns 8–12, anchored to the lower third, a closing line of three to five words at about 3.4vw in a light weight, a paragraph of two or three lines at 17px, and one filled button in the paper colour with ink text, about 52px tall. If the image behind the text is not calm enough, darken the whole photograph slightly with `filter: brightness(0.8)` rather than laying a panel behind the words. The section butts directly against a footer in one solid colour, so the photograph's bottom edge is a hard line. No logo, no second action.
sections.mobile: The photograph is 100vw by 70svh, cropped to keep its subject. The text leaves the image and sits beneath it on the footer's solid colour: closing line at 28px, paragraph at 17px, full-width button. Image and colour meet at a hard edge.

sections.name: Photograph half, menu half
sections.blueprint: A split footer one viewport tall. The left half is a single photograph filling columns 1–6 edge to edge, cropped hard by the left and bottom viewport edges: a close crop of the page's main subject, larger than it appeared anywhere above. The right half, on a flat field, is the site's menu set large: five or six section names stacked as links at about 2.6vw bold, 28px apart, starting at column 8 and 80px from the top. Rows are separated by space only; on hover a row's label shifts right by 12px and the others drop to the softer ink. Under the menu, 64px lower, two short blocks at 15px side by side: contact and social. The legal line runs along the very bottom of the right half at 12px. The wordmark sits small at the top of the right half, on the menu's left edge.
sections.mobile: The photograph leads at full width and 50svh, cropped tight. The menu follows on the flat field at 8vw per item with 20px between items, then contact and social stacked at 15px, then the legal line at 12px. The wordmark sits small above the menu.

references.name: Rafael Derolez
references.idea: A portfolio as a phone carousel: a fixed text rail on the left narrates whichever phone-shaped screen is centred on the right.
references.hero: Dark charcoal page split by a vertical hairline at 30% width. Left rail: a 55px header row with name, slash and current section as a breadcrumb in 16px sans, plus a small cobalt ticket-shaped hire button with a perforated divider and arrow; below a hairline, four short paragraphs of 16px grey text with white links, top-aligned, leaving the lower 40% of the rail empty. Right 70%: three phone-proportioned frames with large rounded corners in a row; the centre one upright, full brightness and about 680px tall, the outer two smaller, dimmed and rotated in perspective toward the centre.
references.type: Suisse at a single 16px size, weight 400, for everything; hierarchy comes only from grey versus white and from the breadcrumb. The one larger setting is a bold two-word line inside the blue contact card. No display type at all.
references.colour: #18181b #030303 #969696 #173ded #ffffff — Zinc-black field with grey text and white for links and the active breadcrumb. Cobalt blue appears only on the hire button and contact card; all other colour comes from the app screenshots.
references.imagery: Phone-shaped frames with large corner radius holding app screens, a selfie and short videos; side frames are dimmed to about 40% and tilted in 3D like a cover-flow.
references.layout: Single viewport, no page scroll: a fixed 432px text rail with 32px padding and a media stage filling the rest. Scrolling advances the carousel and replaces the rail's text; hairlines separate rail, header and stage. On mobile the stage stacks above the rail.

sections.description: Same two-part frame. The breadcrumb's last word changes to the project name; under the header sit three tiny grey meta tags (employer, platform), then two paragraphs. On the stage the centred phone shows the product screen at full brightness while neighbours show the previous and next items dimmed and tilted, so the carousel works as both navigation and preview.

In the rail, a cobalt card shaped like a ticket with notched sides: tiny labels top-left and top-right, a large bold two-word heading, name and local time in small text, then a perforated lower strip with email at left and a copy button at right. Under it, a career list: company in white with dates in small grey on one line, role on the next, and a small arrow at the far right of each row.

steal: Use a breadcrumb (name / current item) as the only heading and update its last word as the content changes.
Show work in device-shaped frames arranged as a cover-flow, with neighbours dimmed and tilted so the next item is always previewed.
Shape the contact card like a ticket with notches and a perforated strip so the one accent-colour element feels like an object.

references.name: Flowjam
references.idea: A persistent frosted sidebar card holds the pitch and buttons while a soft-serif content column scrolls past it; beyond that there is no idea stronger than proof by logos and videos.
references.hero: Grainy off-white page. A tall rounded card about 26% of the viewport wide is pinned at the left and runs off the bottom; frosted over blurred pink and yellow flowers, it holds the logo, a two-line serif tagline, a short blurb and two pill buttons in hot pink and charcoal. The main column starts 32% from the left: a hot-pink pill badge, a three-line serif headline at 4.2vw, then a paragraph whose first sentence is grey and the rest black. A lone charcoal pill button floats far right at mid-height. Below: a heart icon with a proof line, then the top of a four-column logo grid with dotted borders.
references.type: Gelica throughout: a soft, slightly bulbous serif at regular weight, 60px headline with tight -0.05em tracking, 16 to 19px body, down to about 9px in the sidebar. One family for everything including buttons keeps the tone warm but flattens the difference between labels and prose.
references.colour: #f8f8f6 #e7e8e4 #1c0f1f #ff4fe0 #0c0c0c #7b3ff2 — Warm paper white with grain, near-black aubergine text and one hot-pink accent used for the badge and primary button; a purple heart appears once. The footer flips to black.
references.imagery: Rounded-corner video thumbnails of founders talking to camera and product UI clips, each with a small round play button bottom-left; monochrome client logos in a dotted-line grid; blurred floral blobs behind the frosted sidebar.
references.layout: A fixed 26% sidebar card at left for the whole scroll; content occupies one column to its right, split into two for video tiles and four for logos. Sections are separated by whitespace only. The footer is a rounded black panel that still leaves the sidebar in place.

sections.description: Four-column grid of client logos drawn with faint dotted cell borders, each cell roughly 240px wide and 115px tall with the logo centred in dark grey monochrome. Sixteen or more logos over four rows, no captions. Above it, a centred line with a purple heart glyph and a sentence whose first word is black and the rest grey serves as the heading.

Two-column grid of video cards. Each card has a header row with the client name in 14px serif and a one-line result in tiny grey beneath it at left, and a small outlined pill link at right; then a 16:9 thumbnail with about 10px radius and a round play button over its bottom-left corner. Cards are divided by hairlines rather than boxes, and some thumbnails are flat type frames instead of photos.

A rounded black panel inset from the page edges, sitting right of the sidebar. Its background is a short phrase repeated in dark-grey serif at about 5vw, rows offset so the words tile like wallpaper. Centred over it: a two-line white serif headline at about 2.5vw and a small stat line. The lower third holds the logo at left and four narrow columns of tiny text.

steal: Pin a narrow card with logo, one-line pitch and both actions beside the scrolling content, so the call to action never leaves the screen and no top nav is needed.
Set one sentence of a paragraph in grey and the rest in black to rank two claims without changing size or weight.
Tile a short phrase as dark-on-black wallpaper behind the footer headline.

references.name: USAvionix
references.idea: A maker of autonomous jet drones explains its product as a single mission played out on scroll: one pinned WebGL camera flies from a lone drone over forested mountains to a swarm, to detection overlays and then to a dark tactical map, while a console readout runs at the edges and three status colours (observed, threat, secured) carry the plot.
references.hero: After a preloader that shows only the dimmed drone silhouette for over 4.5s, a full-bleed real-time scene: photoreal forested mountains seen from above with a matte black flying wing dead centre, wingspan about 560px (39% of the width). A three-line claim at 80px (5.6vw), Geist 600, -0.04em, leading 0.95, sits top-left at x=32, y 88-300; a three-line 29px lead is docked bottom-right (x 874-1384) over a translucent grey pill about 248x40 that prompts the scroll. A grey contact pill and a menu button are fixed top-right, and a one-word chapter code with sliding tick rails sits top-centre. The middle 60% belongs to the scene.
references.type: Two faces from one superfamily. Geist (41% of characters) at 600 for heads: 80px in the hero (5.6vw, leading 0.95, -0.04em), 76px chapter titles, 50px post-story heads; 29px leads at 500 and 17-19px body. Geist Mono (59%) at 11-12px uppercase, +0.06em, for the telemetry. Sentence case except the mono. The house version keeps Geist alone and sets the readout in sentence case at 16px with tabular figures.
references.colour: #000000 #0f0f0f #ffffff #7aebff #ff6666 #ffcb47 — A black page and near-black scene ground with white text, and three status accents with one job each: amber for observed and the detection boxes, coral for threat, cyan for secured, each under 5% of the text and never on chrome. The terrain brings olive and slate; the closing cards bring warm orange.
references.imagery: Real-time photoreal terrain in a cool, desaturated olive and slate grade with volumetric haze; a matte black flying-wing drone; flat 1px overlay props (bounding boxes with confidence labels, ID tags joined by dotted lines, a sensor cone, curved flight trails, ripple rings); a satellite-style photograph of a village; then warm sunset and dusk renders of a wildfire, a desert ridge and a substation as the payoff.
references.layout: One full-bleed sticky canvas carries 14 chapters over about 60,000px of runway (about 4500px each), with text docked in the corners at 32px margins: title top-left, lead bottom-left or bottom-right at most about 500px wide, telemetry bottom-right, chapter code top-centre. After the story the page returns to normal flow on black for an expanding three-card row and a split with a wireframe globe; margins drift from 32 to 40 to 48px. 72 screens for 435 words.

sections.description: The camera pulls back to three drones in a loose triangle, each with a small white ID tag, the tags joined by dotted lines; a 76px two-line title top-left and, bottom-right from x=732, a 29px lead over a four-row spec table with a label column and lighter values.

Detection: back over the terrain, about 25 small yellow bounding boxes (40-60px) with label chips naming an object class and a confidence percentage, the drone small at the centre, and a four-line readout bottom-right with coordinates, altitude, speed and counts.

A tactical map: a #0f0f0f ground with a faint perspective grid, an irregular outline of a land area covering about 40% of the width, a tag on its edge and three hotspots with 6s ripple rings. Over three chapters the hotspots and tag change colour (amber for survey, coral for threat, cyan for services on site) as grey drone glyphs fly in on curved trails.

After the dark story, three photographic renders in a row from x=48 to 1392 with 24px gaps: one open card 660px wide and two closed at 318px, all about 628px tall with about 10px corners, the open one carrying a 29px title and a three-line 15px description bottom-left.

steal: Tell a product's capability as one pinned scene: about 4500px of scroll per chapter, the camera moving continuously and the text still, changing only by opacity (out over 250ms, in over 400ms after a 200ms delay).

Give colour a job: three status accents, each tied to one state of the story and used only on tags, hotspots and single status words, never on chrome, each under 5% of the text, on black with white type.

After a cold, dark story, pay off with warm photographs in normal flow: an expanding row of three, one open at about 660px and two closed at about 318px. The site speaks in monospace telemetry over hairline grids; the house version sets the readout in the text face with tabular figures and lets the scene carry the structure.
references.media: One sticky full-bleed WebGL scene covers 100% of every story screen, with an SVG overlay drawing the boxes, tags, trails and ripple rings over it; after the story come three photographic mission cards and a wireframe globe bleeding off the right and bottom edges. Two canvases, four images, no video.
references.motion: A preloader of 4.5s or more shows only the dimmed model, then Lenis drives one pinned canvas through about 60,000px: the drone turns from banked to top-down, the camera pulls back to the formation, rises into the mesh, dives to a sensor view and cuts to the map, where zone colours change by chapter. Text moves by opacity only through 346 WAAPI fades (250ms ease-out, 400ms ease-in-out after 200ms), HUD marks transform over 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), 64 ripple rings loop on 6s, and there is no reduced-motion rule.
